newsitem.title: USA: Unisys profits helped by year-long restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Unisys profits helped by year-long restructuring.

text.p: Unisys Corp. reported a profit Wednesday as a costly restructuring launched a year ago continued to help improve operations.

The company, based in Blue Bell, Pa., earned $43.6 million, or 8 cents per share, in the fourth quarter, compared with a loss of $676.8 million, or $4.12 per share, a year earlier. Revenues fell to $1.81 billion from $1.87 billion.
The latest results included a one-time charge of $12.1 million, or 7 cents per share, for early retirement of debt.

Unisys plunged into losses in the 1995 period after taking special charges of $670.5 million, or $3.90 per share, for restructuring measures as well as a loss of $9.8 million from discontinued operations.

"The company has made good financial progress under the three-business structure launched a year ago (under the restructuring). Every quarter in 1996 showed improvement over the one before," said James Unruh, Unisys chairman and chief executive.

"Net income turned positive in the second quarter and grew each subsequent quarter, culminating in a return to profitability on an earnings-per-share basis in the fourth quarter. Our fourth-quarter operating income as a percentage of revenue was the highest in three years."
Unisys said it is on track toward achieving its goal of saving $600 million a year by the end of this year as a result of the restructuring announced in the 1995 fourth quarter.

Unisys said severance costs in the programme have been lower than expected, allowing the company to reverse certain 1995 restructuring reserves in the 1996 fourth quarter. However, this was offset by charges of $84 million to refocus and discontinue certain products and programmes, it said.
Unisys said its Global Customer Services unit's revenues continued to grow, led by its distributed computing support services business.
As expected, revenue in the Information Services Group fell as the unit constrained growth in certain markets and continued to focus on improving profitability, it said.

The Computer Systems Group also made excellent progress in shipping previously delayed models of new enterprise servers, although the unit's revenue declined as expected in the quarter as it continued its product transition, Unisys said.

Unisys said total worldwide orders fell slightly from year-ago levels, and an increase in international orders was offset by a decline in the United States. Order gains were strongest in large-scale enterprise servers and distributed computing support services, it said.
